s1.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: Several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT with contrast
Postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Increased abscess size with globe compression on follow-up CT
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: Several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis

Increased abscess size with globe compression on follow-up CT
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI

shortlist.label: Lacrimal sac abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging studies confirmed left-sided lacrimal sac abscess

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of orbital pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation

shortlist.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of symptoms and absence of clear infectious cause

shortlist.label: Orbital apex syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements and vision loss

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Potential complication of lacrimal sac abscess with risk of intracranial spread

raw.rationale: The presence of a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT with contrast and increased abscess size with globe compression on follow-up CT supports this diagnosis as a more specific subtype of orbital cellulitis.

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: Too broad, as the specific finding of a lacrimal sac abscess points to a more defined condition.

rejected.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
rejected.why: Lack of specific evidence pointing to an idiopathic cause, as the lacrimal sac abscess provides a clear source of infection.

rejected.label: Orbital apex syndrome
rejected.why: The clinical findings and imaging do not indicate involvement of the orbital apex.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: No evidence of cavernous sinus involvement on imaging studies.
